bug_semantics: The OAuth login endpoint accepts a caller-controlled redirect_uri and signs it into the state JWT without validating it. At callback, parseAndValidateClientRedirect treats an administrator allowlist entry as matched when only scheme and host match, ignoring path, query, and fragment; the callback then appends a credential-bearing value to that attacker-chosen same-origin URL. In the disclosed flow that value is a 60-second one-time code accepted by public POST /api/auth/exchange for access and refresh tokens, so leakage through an attacker-selected path, Referer/analytics, or a same-host open redirect yields account takeover.
flaw_origin: ca4e6e05962183206c1c144cf37cb84914c6d800 first introduced the advisory's flawed allowlist mechanism in internal/service/user/user.go: parseAndValidateClientRedirect parsed configured return URLs but compared only redirectURL.Scheme/Host to allowURL.Scheme/Host with strings.EqualFold. Its parent had an older unvalidated redirect flow, but neither this validator nor the path-omitting comparison existed there; ca4e6e is the smallest commit that wrote the specific partial-validation mechanism. 04f7b65d02a4a6e7dc36f0e9a7eccc6dc51df759 later moved that function into internal/service/auth/auth.go and evolved delivery to the exchange-code flow, so it is not the BIC.
ai_marker: absent — the exact ca4e6e05962183206c1c144cf37cb84914c6d800 commit object has author and committer L1nSn0w <l1nsn0w@qq.com> and message 'Enhance OAuth2 and WebAuthn configurations with new settings'; it has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI, or bot trailer/identity.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/lin-snow/Ech0/security/advisories/GHSA-p64j-f4x9-wq66 (repository API https://api.github.com/repos/lin-snow/Ech0/security-advisories/GHSA-p64j-f4x9-wq66) names internal/service/auth/auth.go:448, explains the scheme+host-only check and unvalidated state-JWT redirect, reports vulnerable range <=4.5.6 and patched version 4.7.3, and links the public /api/auth/exchange attack. History: `git log -L` follows the validator through the later auth.go move to ca4e6e05962183206c1c144cf37cb84914c6d800, whose diff adds internal/service/user/user.go parseAndValidateClientRedirect and the exact `strings.EqualFold(redirectURL.Scheme, allowURL.Scheme) && strings.EqualFold(redirectURL.Host, allowURL.Host)` condition; commit URL https://github.com/lin-snow/Ech0/commit/ca4e6e05962183206c1c144cf37cb84914c6d800. Direct-parent proof: `git grep` for both parseAndValidateClientRedirect and that scheme comparator at d6d23f60b349f12679c18e1ff62b7742281c583c returned no matches, while ca4e6e's diff adds the entire 42-line function. The earlier f86d7633ecf92e56292b2260b81d9110892d198b had introduced an unvalidated redirect_uri flow; ca4e6e is nevertheless the first commit encoding the advisory's administrator-allowlist bypass. `git log -S` shows 04f7b65d02a4a6e7dc36f0e9a7eccc6dc51df759 merely carries the same comparison from internal/service/user/user.go into internal/service/auth/auth.go, so it was rejected as a move/refactor BIC. Release checks: v3.1.4 has no comparator; v4.0.0 has it at internal/service/user/user.go:856; v4.5.6 has it at internal/service/auth/auth.go:478; and v4.7.2 still has it at auth.go:481. Thus repository tags show the specific host-only mechanism from v4.0.0 through v4.7.2, exposing that the advisory's <=4.5.6 package range omits still-vulnerable v4.6.x/v4.7.0-v4.7.2. Fix commit a7e8b8e84bd1e3db090dfb720f2c6c433356b442 (https://github.com/lin-snow/Ech0/commit/a7e8b8e84bd1e3db090dfb720f2c6c433356b442) changes internal/service/auth/auth.go to normalize and compare scheme+host+path, adds pre-state validation in BindOAuth and GetOAuthLoginURL, and adds a path-mismatch regression test. `git tag --contains` places that fix first in v4.7.3; v4.7.3 contains `allowNorm := strings.ToLower(allowURL.Scheme)` at auth.go:505 and no longer contains the host-only condition. BIC-only attribution: `git cat-file -p ca4e6e05962183206c1c144cf37cb84914c6d800` shows only the human author/committer and no AI marker. PR association https://github.com/lin-snow/Ech0/pull/160 shows ca4e6e as an ordinary member commit merged by a two-parent merge, not a squash aggregate.
reasoning: The disclosed defect is not merely that a redirect exists; it is that the newly configurable administrator allowlist promises to constrain return URIs but ca4e6e05962183206c1c144cf37cb84914c6d800 enforces only origin equality. The direct parent already accepted redirects without this allowlist, which is relevant lifecycle context, but it did not contain the advisory's partial validator or vulnerable comparison. ca4e6e is therefore the smallest commit that first wrote the exact flawed mechanism. The vulnerable validator survived subsequent changes: 04f7b65d02a4a6e7dc36f0e9a7eccc6dc51df759 moved it to auth.go and paired redirects with a one-time exchange code; neither change constrained attacker-selected same-host paths. a7e8b8e84bd1e3db090dfb720f2c6c433356b442 directly removes the faulty comparison, requires scheme+host+path equality, and rejects bad redirects before signing state, with v4.7.3 as the first containing release. Exact parent-tree absence, source lineage, and tag containment close the causal chain. Because the BIC commit object is authored and committed by L1nSn0w and contains no AI/bot marker or trailer, the BIC-only verdict is NOT_AI; advisory finder credit to aisafe-bot is not BIC authorship evidence.
